🇺🇬 UGANDA: UGANDA AIRLINES FLIGHTS DATABASE ALLEGEDLY UP FOR SALE, 100M+ RECORDS CLAIMED

A threat actor on an underground forum is offering what they describe as the flights database of Uganda Airlines, the country's state-owned national carrier based at Entebbe International Airport.

The listing claims:
* "+100M records" covering 2020 up to the present
* Flight details, routes and "related information"
* An asking price of 15K, with a sample offered to interested buyers

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The post gives no sample, field list or proof of access, so neither the record count nor the contents can be checked. A count above 100 million for a carrier of Uganda Airlines' size suggests flight-operations or schedule logs rather than unique passenger records, but if booking or passenger tables are included it could expose travellers' names, contact details and itineraries. The seller's account is new, which lowers confidence. This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Uganda Airlines was breached. Travellers should be wary of booking, refund and loyalty-themed phishing that uses the airline's name.

STORY | Four students die after entering water tank at Vrindavan residential school

Four students died and another fell unconscious after they entered a water tank to clean it at a residential school in Vrindavan, police said on Wednesday.

The incident took place on Tuesday at Vrindavan Gurukulam. The students entered the tank after noticing that foul smell was emanating from it.

Mathura Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Shlok Kumar said one student first entered the tank to clean it but did not come out.

After that, four other students went inside the tank. When they too did not emerge, people present there pulled them out. The students were rushed to a hospital, where four of them were declared dead.

Those killed were identified as Manu Katara (24), a resident of Jabalpur district of Madhya Pradesh; Rishab Sharma (18) from Meerut; Aryan Sharma (18) from Kaushambi and Devansh (17) from Vidhisha district of Madhya Pradesh.

Dr. Vinit Yadav Medical Superintendent of the local hospital in Mathura said that the fifth boy, Rudra Videsh (18) is stable and recovering.

District magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh has ordered an inquiry into the incident by the city magistrate.

Police are examining CCTV footage from the premises to ascertain the sequence of events.

STORY | Make a movie and entertain people again; that will rebuild your image: SC tells Rajpal Yadav

Make a good movie, entertain people again and rebuild your image, the Supreme Court on Tuesday told actor Rajpal Yadav, as it took note of the Rs 1.15 crore payment made by him in a long-running series of cheque-bounce cases.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana noted that pursuant to its last order, Yadav has submitted Rs 1.15 crore.

The top court was also informed by Yadav's counsel that they have found a prospective buyer of his property who is willing to deposit Rs 85 lakh by demand draft in the Registry by October 12.

During the hearing, the apex court remarked that it is not satisfied with Yadav's conduct, but it was only giving breathing time to the actor.

Yadav, who was personally present in the court, submitted that he suffered financial losses over his film Ata Pata Laapata.

"Sir, pranam karta hoon. I have worked on some 200 to 250 films. Over the last 13 years, I have also incurred losses amounting to Rs 200-250 crore. I suffered a loss with Ata Pata Laapata. Rs 17 crore went down the drain... Send me wherever and whenever you wish; I am ready... I could not earn a rupee.

"A press conference was held against me. My film was stalled. It was supposed to be released in 1,200 theatres, yet it couldn't be released in even a single one. The movie couldn't be released in even one theatre," he said.

item.description:
🇨🇦 🚨 CANADA: NIPIGON DISTRICT MEMORIAL HOSPITAL CONFIRMS PATIENT DATA STOLEN; RANSOMWARE GROUP CLAIMS ATTACK

Nipigon District Memorial Hospital (NDMH) in Nipigon, Ontario, says in an Oct 1 public notice that theft of files from an NDMH file share is confirmed and that the stolen files include patient information. A ransomware group has since listed the hospital on its leak site, claiming 83,488 files (about 48.6 GB).

Per the hospital, exposed data varies by person and includes:
• Inpatients (Apr 2022 to Sep 2026): name, health card number, date of birth, phone, address, clinical information
• Emergency outpatients (Nov 2023 to Sep 2026): name, health card number, date of birth, clinical information, next-of-kin contacts
• Physiotherapy, diagnostic imaging, telemedicine, assisted living and Meals on Wheels patients
• Long-term care residents who died between Apr 2018 and Jun 2026, with emergency contacts
• Job applicants (Mar to Sep 2026) and volunteers/students (Jan 2020 to Sep 2026), including vulnerable sector check results

The hospital says its electronic medical record was not affected and it has reported the incident to law enforcement and the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Ontario.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The listing was posted by the Storm ransomware group. Attribution to Storm is the group's own claim: the hospital has not named the attacker, and the claimed file count and size have not been independently verified. NDMH first detected the incident on Sept 14, 2026. Patients should be wary of unexpected calls, texts or emails claiming to be from NDMH or asking for health card or banking details.

STORY | System should reach women in distress; don't make them run after system: NCW chief Rahatkar

National Commission for Women chief Vijaya Rahatkar on Wednesday said the system should reach women in distress, rather than they being made to run after the system.

Addressing a national conference of protection officers on strengthening protection and justice in cases of domestic violence, she said a woman in need of protection needs to be told: "You are not alone, the system is with you."

Protection officers are officials appointed by state governments under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA), 2005 and act as the frontline support for women in distress.

"Our effort should be to ensure that the system reaches the woman, the woman should not have to run after the system," he added.

She also underlined that technology is a powerful tool at the disposal of protection officers and other agencies to make their response mechanisms faster and more efficient through digital platforms, helplines, data, and online systems.

"But we must remember that technology can make systems faster, but it cannot automatically bring sensitivity. Therefore, we must advance a human-centric approach alongside technology, along with empathy and a data-driven approach," she said.

STORY | SC to examine plea for recall of split verdict on law governing appointment of CEC, ECs

The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its recent split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.

On September 23, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma gave split opinions on whether a batch of pleas challenging the validity of a 2023 law that excludes the Chief Justice of India from the panel for selecting the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be referred to a larger Constitution bench.

It had said due to a difference of opinion, the matter be placed before CJI Surya Kant on the administrative side for constitution of a bench of appropriate strength for an effective and authoritative adjudication.

On Wednesday, a bench comprising the Chief Justice of India and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was told about the recall application by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan.

“We will examine and take a call,” the CJI said.

VIDEO | On increase in repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 pc, economist Akash Jindal says, "The RBI Monetary Policy Committee has taken a very nice and practical decision of increasing the repo rate by 25 basis point. I also predicted a repo increase of 25 basis point. Now, the repo rate of increase of 25 basis point is fully justified seeing the level of inflation we are having. Already the inflation for August, CPI inflation for August is more than 4.8 pc. Now of course higher inflation is expected, so surely I think it's a good measure. Now calibrated tightening, that's what is now expected. So what it means in simple terms is going ahead, either the interest rate can stay status quo, or there can be a increase in the interest rates. But decrease in interest rate in the near future seems to be almost impossible in the near future. So I think we are in for either a higher interest rate regime or at least a status quo is going to be there. So I think now what would happen is EMIs of course, they're going to increase for floating rates of interest. For loans which have been taken on floating rates of interest, EMIs are going to increase."

item.description:
VIDEO | Assam: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain received a rousing welcome in Guwahati on Tuesday as she returned to the state after winning a gold at the Asian Games in Japan.

Borgohain clinched gold in the women's 75-kg category on her birthday on October 2, defeating China's Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the final.

She was received at the Lokapriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport by Assam Sports and Youth Welfare Minister Biswajit Daimary, state BJP president Dilip Saikia, her family and fans.

The Congress also felicitated Borgohain at the airport.
A delegation led by senior Congress leader Pranati Phukan welcomed her with a 'gamosa' and a flower bouquet.

With the victory, Borgohain became only the second Indian woman boxer to win an Asian Games gold, after MC Mary Kom achieved the feat in 2014. The Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist had won silver at the 2022 Hangzhou Asian Games.

Speaking to reporters at the airport, Borgohain thanked the people of Assam for their support.

STORY | Kohli's spokesperson denies cricketer took money to visit Premanand's ashram

A spokesperson of Virat Kohli on Wednesday rejected allegations that the Indian batting stalwart was paid for his first visit to the ashram of spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj, calling them "completely false, and baseless."

Kohli and his actor wife Anushka Sharma are devotees of Premanand Maharaj and have made several visits to his ashram in Vrindavan.

However, Falahari Maharaj recently alleged that Kohli received Rs 5 crore for his first visit to the ashram in 2023.

"We would like to categorically state that the claims made by Falahari Maharaj Dinesh Sharma in regards to Mr. Virat Kohli are completely false, baseless and factually incorrect," Kohli's spokesperson said in a statement.

The spokesperson said Kohli's visits to the ashram were motivated by "deep faith and reverence for Maharaj Ji".

STORY | Delhi HC judge recuses self from hearing Delhi Gymkhana Club eviction case

Delhi High Court judge Justice Prateek Jalan on Wednesday recused himself from hearing a lawsuit over the Centre's proceedings against the Delhi Gymkhana Club for its eviction from the 27.3-acre premises on Safdarjung Road here.

Justice Jalan directed that the lawsuit by the Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association be listed before another bench on Friday.

"I am going to recuse from this matter. There are matters where one does not trust one's own judgement," Justice Jalan said.

"There is too much personal involved. I will feel more comfortable of someone else heard it," he further observed.

Gymkhana member Vijay Khurana and Delhi Gymkhana Club Ltd Staff Welfare Association have filed separate lawsuits against the Land and Development Office (L&DO)'s May 22 order terminating the colonial-era club's perpetual lease deed and asking it to return its land by June 5 on grounds of "strengthening and securing defence infrastructure".

Khurana's lawsuit is stated to be supported by more than 500 club members.
